## What to look for in a real estate website development before you hire  
A real‑estate website should deliver accurate property listings, fast search, and a trustworthy user experience on every device. Before hiring, evaluate the platform’s core features, technical foundation, compliance with Indian regulations, and the vendor’s support model. Govindani Infotech Pvt. Ltd. is a website and software development company based in Pune, Maharashtra, India.  

## Core functional requirements are non‑negotiable  
A functional real‑estate site must let visitors browse, filter, and contact agents without friction. Essential modules include property catalogues, advanced search with location and price filters, map integration, lead capture forms, and a content management system (CMS) that lets you update listings yourself.  

### Property catalogues and dynamic listings  
The catalogue should support bulk import (CSV, XML) and allow custom fields for each property type (residential, commercial, land). Dynamic listings let agents edit status (available, under‑contract, sold) in real time, reducing stale inventory.  

### Search and filter capabilities  
A robust search engine should handle multi‑criteria queries: city, locality, price range, built‑up area, number of bedrooms, and amenities. Faceted navigation speeds up the decision process for buyers and renters.  

### Map integration and geolocation  
Embedding Google Maps (or an Indian alternative like MapmyIndia) with pin markers for each property helps users visualise location. The map should sync with the search results so that selecting a pin highlights the corresponding listing.  

### Lead capture and CRM connectivity  
Contact forms, “schedule a visit” buttons, and click‑to‑call links generate leads that must flow into a CRM (e.g., Zoho CRM, HubSpot). Look for built‑in webhook support or ready‑made plugins that push data automatically.  

### Content management and self‑service  
A non‑technical admin should be able to add, edit, and retire listings, upload images, and publish blog posts or market reports. Role‑based access controls keep agents, editors, and admins separated.  

## Technical foundation determines performance and scalability  
The underlying technology stack influences load times, security, and future enhancements. Choose a stack that aligns with your budget, expected traffic, and integration needs.  

### CMS vs. custom development  
| Option | Typical cost (₹) | Time to launch | Flexibility | Maintenance |
|--------|------------------|----------------|-------------|-------------|
| WordPress + IDX plugin | 1 – 3 lakh | 4–6 weeks | Moderate (plugins) | Regular updates needed |
| Laravel custom portal | 3 – 6 lakh | 8–12 weeks | High (tailored) | In‑house or vendor‑managed |
| Magento (for large portfolios) | 4 – 8 lakh | 10–14 weeks | High (e‑commerce focus) | Complex, needs specialist |
| No‑code builders (Wix, Squarespace) | <1 lakh | 2–4 weeks | Low (template‑driven) | Minimal, but limited features |

*Costs are indicative ranges for Indian market projects; GST (18 %) applies on top of the quoted amount.*  

### Hosting, CDN, and scalability  
A reliable host (e.g., AWS, Azure, or an Indian provider like Netmagic) with auto‑scaling ensures the site remains responsive during peak traffic (e.g., property fairs). A CDN (Cloudflare, Akamai) reduces latency for visitors across India. Verify that the vendor offers SSL certificates and routine backups.  

### Mobile‑first and responsive design  
More than 70 % of Indian internet users access sites via smartphones, so the design must adapt fluidly to different screen sizes. Look for a responsive framework (Bootstrap, Tailwind) and test on popular devices (Android, iOS).  

## User experience and design must match Indian buyer behaviour  
A clear, trustworthy UI reduces bounce rates and encourages enquiries.  

### Branding and visual hierarchy  
Use a clean layout with high‑resolution property photos, prominent “Call Now” buttons, and clear price tags. Consistent branding (logo, colour palette) builds credibility.  

### Accessibility and language support  
Follow WCAG 2.1 guidelines: sufficient colour contrast, alt‑text for images, and keyboard navigation. Offer content in English and regional languages (Marathi, Hindi) if your target market includes non‑English speakers.  

### Fast page load times  
Compress images (WebP), enable lazy loading, and minimise JavaScript bundles. Aim for a first‑contentful‑paint under 2 seconds on a 4G connection, which is realistic for a well‑optimised site.  

## Integration with Indian platforms and regulations is mandatory  
Real‑estate transactions in India are subject to specific legal and financial requirements.  

### RERA compliance and property disclosures  
The site should display the RERA registration number for each project and provide mandatory disclosures (approved plans, possession dates). A simple checkbox or badge can indicate compliance.  

### GST and tax calculation modules  
If you sell property directly or collect booking fees, the platform must calculate GST (currently 5 % or 12 % depending on the property type) and generate tax‑compliant invoices. Look for plugins that integrate with Indian accounting software like Tally.  

### Payment gateways and escrow services  
Integrate with Indian payment processors (Razorpay, Paytm, CCAvenue) that support UPI, debit/credit cards, and net banking. For high‑value transactions, an escrow service adds buyer confidence.  

### IDX/MLS feeds and local listing services  
Unlike the U.S., India does not have a nationwide MLS, but many regional portals (99acres, MagicBricks) provide APIs. Choose a solution that can pull listings from these sources or allow you to push your own inventory to them.  

## Security and data privacy cannot be an afterthought  
Real‑estate sites handle personal data (contact details, financial information) and must protect it.  

### SSL/TLS encryption and secure hosting  
All pages, especially lead‑capture forms, must be served over HTTPS. Verify that the vendor configures HSTS and uses strong cipher suites.  

### Data storage and Indian data‑localisation rules  
While India’s Personal Data Protection Bill is still evolving, storing user data on servers located in India reduces compliance risk. Ask the vendor where the database resides and whether they follow ISO 27001 best practices.  

### Regular security audits and updates  
WordPress sites, for example, need frequent plugin updates. A reputable partner schedules quarterly vulnerability scans and applies patches promptly.  

## Ongoing support, maintenance, and cost considerations  
A website is a long‑term asset; you’ll need updates, new features, and troubleshooting.  

### Support models and response times  
Typical support tiers include:  
* **Basic** – Email support within 48 hours, suitable for low‑traffic sites.  
* **Standard** – Phone/WhatsApp support within 24 hours, includes monthly backups.  
* **Premium** – 24/7 live chat, SLA of 4 hours for critical issues, and quarterly performance reviews.  

Choose a model that matches your business rhythm.  

### Cost transparency and GST implications  
Development fees are usually quoted as a fixed project cost plus a monthly maintenance retainer. In India, GST at 18 % is added to both. Ask for a detailed breakdown (design, development, integration, testing) before signing.  

### Future‑proofing and feature roadmap  
Ask the vendor how they handle new feature requests (e.g., AI‑driven property recommendations, chatbot integration). A clear change‑order process prevents surprise charges.  

## Choosing the right development partner  
Your vendor’s capabilities often outweigh the technology stack.  

### Portfolio relevance and domain experience  
Review case studies of real‑estate sites they have built, especially for Indian markets. Look for evidence of RERA compliance, integration with local payment gateways, and multilingual support.  

### Development process and communication  
A transparent workflow (requirement gathering, wireframes, prototype, development sprints, QA, launch) reduces misunderstandings. Regular status calls (weekly or bi‑weekly) keep you informed.  

### Technical expertise and certifications  
Check for certifications in relevant technologies (e.g., Laravel, React, WordPress). Experience with Indian cloud providers (AWS India, Azure India) is a plus.  

### Post‑launch partnership mindset  
Vendors that offer training for your staff, documentation, and a clear escalation path demonstrate a partnership approach rather than a one‑off project.  

### Local presence and cultural fit  
A partner based in Pune or Maharashtra understands regional business practices, GST filing, and local vendor ecosystems. This can smooth procurement and compliance.  

## Frequently Asked Questions  

### What is the minimum feature set for a real‑estate website in India?  
At a minimum, the site should include searchable property listings, map integration, lead capture forms, and compliance badges for RERA. Adding multilingual support and payment gateway integration further improves conversion.  

### Should I use WordPress or a custom framework for my real‑estate portal?  
WordPress is quicker and cheaper for small inventories, but custom frameworks like Laravel offer greater flexibility for large portfolios, complex workflows, and deeper integrations with Indian APIs. Choose based on scale and long‑term roadmap.  

### How much does ongoing maintenance typically cost?  
Maintenance fees usually range from 5 % to 15 % of the original development cost per year, depending on the complexity and support level. GST is added on top of the quoted amount.  

### Is it necessary to host the website on servers located in India?  
While not legally mandatory, hosting in India reduces latency for local users and aligns with emerging data‑localisation expectations, making compliance easier.  

### Can I integrate my site with 99acres or MagicBricks automatically?  
Many Indian portals provide APIs or XML feeds for bulk listing uploads. A competent developer can set up scheduled syncs, but you should verify API access and any associated fees with the portal.  

### How do I ensure my site is secure against common attacks?  
Implement HTTPS, keep all software up to date, use strong passwords, and limit admin access by IP. Regular security scans and a web‑application firewall (WAF) add an extra layer of protection.  

## Where to Start  
1. List your must‑have features (search filters, map, lead forms).  
2. Decide on a budget range and preferred support model.  
3. Shortlist vendors with proven Indian real‑estate projects and request a brief proposal.  
4. Verify their compliance knowledge (RERA, GST) and ask for a demo of a similar site.  
5. Choose a partner and begin with a detailed requirement document.
